newsitem.title: USA: Innovo Group sees Q3 sales up 44 pct.
newsitem.headline: Innovo Group sees Q3 sales up 44 pct.

text.p: Innovo Group Inc said Wednesday it expects to post a 44 percent gain in third quarter sales, due in part to sales of Olympic team licensed products.
Innovo, which manufactures sports bags and T-shirts, said it expects sales for the third quarter ending August 31 to be about $2.36 million, up from $1.64 million a year ago.
Sales for the first nine months of fiscal 1996 are expected to be $5.76 million, up 44.4 percent from last year, the company said.
Third quarter sales increases, however, were partially offset by labor shortages in both Tennessee and Georgia, the company said.
Innovo said labor shortages were continuing to limit Innovo's production, but the company had gradually been adding sewers and was exploring means of insuring adequate labor supplies in the future.
Innovo declined comment on operating results for the three and nine months ending August 31.

The results will be affected by the sales lost to the labor shortage, as well as by the money Innovo is spending to develop the products to be marketed under the company's new Warner Bros, Anheuser-Busch and Gary Patterson licenses, Innovo said.
Sales of these licensed products are expected to start in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996, with the impact projected to start in the second quarter of fiscal 1997, the company said.
